summary.en: Drone attacks linked to Ethiopia killed four people and damaged a United Nations building in Khartoum, while artillery shelling in Alamata killed 14 civilians. Ethiopia has offered to host comprehensive Sudanese dialogue and Abiy Ahmed has called for Sudanese parties to join a mediation table, while leaked intelligence suggests Eritrean and Sudanese coordination of drone strikes on Mekelle and Assosa. Ethiopian forces have regained control of border areas near Badme, and fighting along the Afar-Somali border continues over territorial disputes, drought and resource scarcity. Amnesty International has called for a probe into possible war crimes in Tigray, and 2,824 battle-related deaths were recorded in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Droneangrep knyttet til Etiopia drepte fire personer og skadet en FN-bygning i Khartoum, mens artilleriskudd i Alamata drepte 14 sivile. Etiopia har tilbudt å være vert for en omfattende sudansk dialog, og Abiy Ahmed har oppfordret sudanske parter til å delta i et meklingstabell, mens lekket etterretning tyder på eritreisk og sudansk koordinering av droneangrep mot Mekelle og Assosa. Etiopiske styrker har gjenvunnet kontrollen over grenseområder nær Badme, og kamper langs grensen mellom Afar og Somali pågår over territorielle tvister, tørke og ressursknapphet. Amnesty International har bedt om en etterforskning av mulige krigsforbrytelser i Tigray, og 2 824 dødsfall knyttet til kamper ble registrert i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Fano insurgency
background.extract: The Fano insurgency or Amhara war is an armed conflict and insurgency in the Amhara Region of Ethiopia that began in April 2023 between the Fano militia and the Ethiopian government. The conflict started after the government attempted to dissolve the Amhara Special Forces and other regional forces as part of a plan to reform and centralize the country's security apparatus, and integrate them into the federal armed forces. This move led to protests and armed resistance by local forces under Fano.
